name: Brocade-Wound
geological_features: Embroidery-like mineral deposits in cooling lava surfaces
Collapsed volcanic calderas forming nested rings
specific_features: Mineral crystallization patterns on lava flows resembling brocade embroidery
Self-healing crust that reseals fractures within hours
description: Brocade-Wound is a volcanic world with an unusual geological characteristic: its lava flows produce intricate surface crystallization patterns as they cool, with mineral deposits forming raised, ornate designs that closely resemble brocade embroidery. These patterns result from the interaction of multiple mineral species crystallizing at different temperatures as the lava surface cools, each mineral preferentially nucleating on the boundaries of previously crystallized species to create layered, interlocking designs of remarkable beauty and complexity.

The planet earned the second half of its name from its other distinguishing feature: a self-healing crust. When tectonic stress fractures the surface, the underlying magma wells up and cools so rapidly that the crack is resealed within hours, leaving a raised scar of fresh brocade-patterned lava. The planet is constantly wounding and healing itself, its surface a palimpsest of old scars overlaid with new patterns. The toxic atmosphere smells of sulfur and hot metal, and the air temperature fluctuates with the ceaseless volcanic activity below.

Microbial life thrives in the hydrothermal fields where superheated water percolates through the porous volcanic rock, bringing dissolved minerals to the surface. These organisms have adapted to temperatures that approach the theoretical limits of biochemistry, and their metabolic byproducts contribute to the mineral crystallization patterns that make the planet's lava flows so distinctive. In a real sense, the brocade patterns are partly biological in origin—life has literally woven itself into the planet's geological processes.

The precious metal deposits in Brocade-Wound's hydrothermal systems are substantial, with gold and silver concentrations in the hot spring deposits exceeding anything found in terrestrial hydrothermal systems. The self-healing nature of the crust presents both opportunity and challenge: mining sites are quickly obliterated by fresh lava flows, but the same process continuously concentrates new mineral deposits at the surface. Adaptive mining strategies using mobile robotic extractors that follow the active hydrothermal zones have proven moderately successful. The planet heals every wound inflicted upon it, layering fresh brocade over the scars, an artist that never stops working and never repeats a pattern.
